rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 is the best design so far (619.4). Oval finishes 20/20 and s-bend finishes 18/20 at base_speed 0.75, kp 5.3, kd 0.8, ki 1.0, 7 sensors at x=+/-0.08 with 0.012 m footprints. Slalom has been flat at progress 0.16-0.17 with 0/20 finishes across iterations 5-8, despite changes to speed, kp, kd and sensor size. Iteration 8 shows that raising sensor_size to 0.016 hurt badly (s-bend fell to 1/20, score 447), so that change is reverted. Iteration 7 shows that kp 6.5 overcorrects the s-bend and does not help slalom. So neither sensor size nor steering gain is the slalom limit. Hypothesis: the integral term (ki 1.0, capped at +/-2, which is up to about 2 turn units of bias) builds up a steering bias on alternating weaves and pushes the robot off at each change of direction. Change: set the geometry back to iteration 6 (sensor_size 0.012, all else unchanged) and reduce ki from 1.0 to 0.6. That still gives enough integral action to cancel the fixed motor mismatch on the oval, which iteration 2 showed was needed, but removes some of the windup on slalom. Everything else stays as in iteration 6, so the result isolates the ki effect. Expected result: oval and s-bend stay near iteration 6 levels (oval about 2.1 s, s-bend finish rate 0.8 or more), with slalom progress above 0.25 if the windup hypothesis holds. Risks: rms_error on the oval may rise slightly if the mismatch is not fully cancelled. If slalom is still flat at about 0.16, the next step is to test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' and a lower base_speed (0.6) on slalom only. If the oval rms rises above 0.02, restore ki to 0.8. Measurements needed: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation, with slalom progress and line_loss_events as the key signals.
